classification.difficultyReason: Direct recognition or a familiar short procedure. The ceiling brackets require the least integer at least π.

content.prompt:
Let $x\in\mathbb R$ and define $\lfloor x\rfloor$ and $\lceil x\rceil$ by
$$\begin{aligned}\lfloor x\rfloor&=\max\{m\in\mathbb Z\text{ where }m\le x\}\\\lceil x\rceil&=\min\{m\in\mathbb Z\text{ where }m\ge x\}\end{aligned}$$
These are respectively called the $\mathit{floor}$ and $\mathit{ceiling}$ of $x$. Find the value of $\lceil\pi\rceil$.

answer.worked: $3<\pi<4$, so the least integer no smaller than $\pi$ is $4$. Hence $\lceil\pi\rceil=4$.
